etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French sobre, from Latin sōbrius, from se- (“without”) + ebrius (“intoxicated”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁egʷʰ- (“drink”). In the sense "not drunk," displaced native undrunken, from Old English undruncen.

definitions.definition: Not under the influence of any recreational drug.

quote.citation: 2014 October 27, Taylor Swift, Imogen Heap, “Clean (Taylor's Version)”, in 1989 (Taylor's Version)‎[1], performed by Taylor Swift, published 2023 October 27:
quote.text: Ten months sober, I must admitJust because you're clean, don't mean you don't miss it

definitions.definition: Not given to excessive drinking of alcohol.

quote.citation: 1890, John Charles Cox, “The Sober Life”, in The Godly, Righteous, And Sober Life, page 35:
quote.text: Amid all the confusion and disorder that sin has introduced into the world, the Christian in union with God has a grace or Divine help that enables him to live the sober, self-restrained life.

quote.citation: 2020 December 29, Hilary Sheinbaum, “Finding Love Without Alcohol”, in The New York Times‎[2], →ISSN:
quote.text: After eliminating alcohol from their lives, some sober individuals exclusively date nondrinkers.

quote.citation: (Can we date this quote?), (Please provide the book title or journal name)‎[3]:
quote.text: Rose told me that she's sober.

definitions.definition: (figurative) Moderate; realistic; serious; not playful; not passionate; cool; self-controlled.

quote.citation: 1678, John Bunyan, The Pilgrim’s Progress from This World, to That which is to Come: […], London:  […]  Nath[aniel] Ponder […], →OCLC, page 31:
quote.text: God help me to watch and to be sober.

quote.citation: 1680, John Dryden, “The Preface to Ovid’s Epistles”, in Ovid, Ovid’s Epistles, […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson […], →OCLC:
quote.text: [N]o ſober man vvould put himſelf into a danger for the Applauſe of ſcaping vvithout breaking his Neck.

quote.citation: 2005, Plato, translated by Lesley Brown, Sophist, page 230d:
quote.text: Which is the finest and soberest state possible.

definitions.definition: (of color) Dull; not bright or colorful.

quote.citation: 1667, John Milton, “(please specify the page number)”, in Paradise Lost. […], London:  […]  [Samuel Simmons], and are to be sold by Peter Parker […]; [a]nd by Robert Boulter […]; [a]nd Matthias Walker, […], →OCLC; republished as Paradise Lost in Ten Books: […], London: Basil Montagu Pickering […], 1873, →OCLC:
quote.text: Twilight grey / Had in her sober livery all things clad.

quote.citation: 1717, Alexander Pope, Letter from Edward Blount, Esq.:
quote.text: See her sober over a sampler, or gay over a jointed baby.

quote.citation: 1718, Mat[thew] Prior, “Alma: Or, The Progress of the Mind”, in Poems on Several Occasions, London:  […]  Jacob Tonson […], and John Barber […], →OCLC:
quote.text: What parts gay France from sober Spain? A little rising rocky chain.

definitions.definition: (often with up) To make or become sober.

quote.citation: 1711, Alexander Pope, An Essay on Criticism:
quote.text: There shallow draughts intoxicate the brain, / And drinking largely sobers us again.

quote.citation: 1950 January, David L. Smith, “A Runaway at Beattock”, in Railway Magazine, page 53:
quote.text: The night air may have sobered him a bit by the time they got back to Beattock.

definitions.definition: (often with up) To overcome or lose a state of intoxication.
To moderate one's feelings; to accept a disappointing reality after losing one's ability to believe in a fantastic goal.
